brief.situation: You are a developer at Penwick Outfitters. The orders service's Cloud Build pipeline runs integration tests against the shared staging Firestore database. Since the team grew, builds run in parallel, and about 40% of them fail with tests reading orders another build created or deleted. Release freeze starts at 17:00, and three fixes still need green builds to ship.
handover: The tests create and delete documents in the orders and inventory collections.
Locally, developers run the tests against the Firestore emulator.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the parallel builds, the shared staging database they all write to, and the emulator each build could run instead.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why builds failed, what you changed, and what keeps tests off real databases.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: CI ran integration tests against the shared staging database; with parallel builds, tests saw and deleted each other's documents. Locally the same tests used the emulator.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: The test step starts the Firestore emulator and sets FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST, so the client connects to it; five parallel builds passed. Pointing at production pollutes it; retries hide the collisions.

parts.label: Real databases
parts.modelAnswer: The build service account lost write access to staging, and test setup fails if the emulator variable is missing.

prodPolluted.headline: Isolate tests; never borrow production
prodPolluted.body: Each build should test against its own database. Production is not an unused test database.

scoring.modelReasoning: Random failures where tests see other tests' data mean shared state: CI runs against the staging database, and parallel builds collide. Start the Firestore emulator in the test step and set FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST, which makes the client connect to it, so each build has its own database; prove it with parallel builds. Pointing at production pollutes production; retries only hide the problem. Then remove CI's write access and guard test setup.
